semantic_observations: A network section writes its two section summary counts first, followed by the block-state paletted container and then the biome paletted container; biome state is therefore part of every serialized section image rather than a separate chunk-side array.

The selected factory resolves the target biome registry, builds the biome strategy over the registry holder-id map, chooses Plains as the default biome, and creates biome containers from that frozen strategy/default pair.

PalettedContainer network writing delegates the concrete palette/storage body to the container data together with the strategy's global id map; the exact configuration and palette encodings remain intentionally owned by the separately reviewed R2C-BIOME-PALETTE-WIRE delegate closure.

For positive-width packed storage, the reviewed SimpleBitStorage constructor uses a value mask of 2^bits-1, packs floor(64/bits) values per 64-bit word, requires ceil(size/valuesPerLong) words, and rejects a supplied raw array of any other length.

Reviewed SimpleBitStorage mutation and unpacking keep values wholly inside individual 64-bit words: sequential logical values occupy successive low-to-high bit slots of each word, and the final word carries only the remaining logical values.

The reviewed packed-storage raw accessor exposes the backing word sequence directly. How the biome paletted-container data layer selects palette modes and emits those words remains intentionally owned by the separately reviewed R2C-BIOME-PALETTE-WIRE delegate closure.
The initial chunk payload copies only heightmap entries whose type usage is CLIENT and clones each selected raw long array before publication.

For 26.2 the client-selected heightmap types are WORLD_SURFACE (wire id 1), MOTION_BLOCKING (wire id 4), and MOTION_BLOCKING_NO_LEAVES (wire id 5); WORLD_SURFACE uses non-air, MOTION_BLOCKING uses motion-blocking or non-empty fluid, and MOTION_BLOCKING_NO_LEAVES additionally excludes leaves.
A heightmap contains exactly 256 column values in a packed storage whose bit width is ceil(log2(chunkHeight+1)); local column (x,z) maps to index x + 16*z.
The stored heightmap value is relative to the chunk minimum Y: setHeight stores firstAvailableY-minY and lookup adds minY back. A zero packed value therefore denotes firstAvailableY == minY.

Priming examines each local x/z column from the highest available section downward and records y+1 at the first block satisfying each requested heightmap predicate; if no matching block is found, that type remains at its zero/minY value.

The chunk payload heightmap field is a map keyed by Heightmap.Types and carrying raw long arrays; it is encoded before the section byte buffer and block-entity list. The reviewed packet constructor snapshots the arrays rather than retaining mutable Heightmap storage.

The light publication lattice has dimensionSectionCount+2 entries, begins at minSectionY-1, and ends at minLightSection+lightSectionCount; packet section index i addresses light section minLightSection+i.
With null changed-section filters the initial light payload considers every light-section index for both SKY and BLOCK layers; a non-null filter limits preparation to its set indices.

For each considered section the packet asks the selected layer listener for nullable DataLayer state. A null result contributes neither a regular nor empty bit; a present empty layer sets the corresponding empty mask; a present non-empty layer sets the regular mask and contributes a copied byte payload.

The exact concrete getDataLayerData lookup and DataLayer empty/materialization semantics are deliberately not inferred by this parent review; they are owned by the independently reviewed R2C-LIGHT-DATA-LAYER delegate closure and must be bound before admission.

The light packet wire body writes sky-present, block-present, empty-sky and empty-block masks in that order, then the sky update collection followed by the block update collection. Individual update byte arrays use the reviewed 2048-byte-bounded codec.

LevelLightEngine selects the block or sky listener for the requested layer, falling back to the dummy listener only when that engine is absent; the production concrete listener choice remains subject to the delegate review rather than being defaulted here.

Stored chunk parsing treats isLightOn as an explicit persisted boolean defaulting false and treats BlockLight and SkyLight independently per section: a present byte array constructs a DataLayer while an absent tag produces no layer.

This parent closure admits only initial light state, span and packet mask/update classification. It does not admit light propagation, world-generation lighting, movement-driven updates, or publication pacing.
